deliverables.content:
Objective deliverable

Launch-week social media plan — Somebody
Status: Draft for review only. Do not publish or send.
Version 3 change: company-record basis re-checked for this review pass; no publishing or sending performed.

1. Verified basis and evidence boundaries

Verified from company records:
- Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It helps organise work, bring in help when needed, and stay with an objective until there is a usable result. (Company profile, company/profile.)
- Signup conversion is weak; visitors do not immediately recognise that the product is for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools. Existing language is broad (“AI manager” and “automate your workflows”). (Launch brief, launch/context.)
- The company does not yet have strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem. (Launch brief, launch/context.)

Evidence gaps:
- No scoped evidence establishes which platform, format, day, or time produces the best reach or engagement for Somebody.
- No scoped audience research establishes platform-specific audience behavior, preferred language, or engagement trends.
- The schedule below is therefore an executable test sequence, not a claim about optimal timing. Record results after each post before changing priorities.

2. Message to use across channels

Core message: “Somebody is an AI manager for founders running a one-person company or lean team—helping important objectives keep moving without adding another tool to manage.”

Supporting points:
- Make the audience explicit: founders carrying several parts of the business.
- Show the outcome in practical terms: organise the work, bring in help when needed, and stay with the objective until there is a usable result.
- Contrast carefully: do not claim Somebody replaces the founder, guarantees a business result, or use unsupported superiority claims.
- Avoid leading with generic “AI manager” or “automate your workflows” language without immediately explaining who it is for and what it does.
- CTA for all launch posts: “See how Somebody works for one-person companies and lean teams.” Use the approved destination link when available.

3. Launch-week sequence (local time; proposed test schedule, not an evidence-based optimal-time claim)

Day 1 — Clarify: publish the audience-and-problem introduction on all four channels, adapted per channel. Reply to genuine questions using only approved product facts.
Day 2 — Demonstrate: publish one concrete objective/workflow example; keep the example truthful and avoid promising a business result.
Day 3 — Explain: publish “what Somebody is / is not,” especially that it supports rather than replaces the founder.
Day 4 — Conversation: publish a question asking founders which important objective keeps slipping; treat responses as exploratory qualitative input, not validated market evidence.
Day 5 — Reframe: publish a concise comparison against generic AI-tool language, focusing on responsibility for moving an objective forward rather than feature superiority.
Day 6 — Proof of use: publish a second example or behind-the-scenes walkthrough using only an approved, real product flow; if no approved flow exists, use a product explanation instead.
Day 7 — Recap and CTA: summarise the clearest message tested during the week and invite qualified founders to review/sign up. Do not describe any message as a winner unless results are measured and reviewed.

Suggested publishing windows for the first test: 09:00 and 16:00 local time, using one primary post per channel per day. These are operating slots chosen to make the test executable, not claims about audience activity. Keep the same windows across the week where feasible so results are comparable. A reviewer may replace them after channel analytics are available.

4. Channel execution

TikTok — priority: short vertical demonstration and founder-context storytelling.
- Format: 20–45 second vertical video; first seconds identify “for founders running a one-person company or lean team.” Show one objective moving from brief to organised next steps, with captions and a clear end card.
- Day 1 script: “If you run the company and carry every important objective, Somebody is an AI manager built to help keep the work moving.”
- Day 2/6: screen-recorded or narrated walkthrough of one approved product flow; redact sensitive information.
- Day 3: direct-to-camera “not a replacement for the founder; a practical way to keep an objective moving.”
- Priority: clarity and demonstration before trend-based creative. No trend, sound, or engagement claim is verified in scope.

Instagram — priority: saveable visual explanation plus short video.
- Format: Reel adapted from the TikTok demonstration, plus a 4–6 panel carousel: audience, recurring burden, what Somebody does, what it does not promise, CTA.
- Caption opening: “Running a one-person company means important work can keep competing for your attention.” Follow with the verified product description, without presenting that sentence as validated customer language.
- Use Stories for a poll or question on Day 4 only as exploratory feedback. Do not treat poll responses as representative audience research.
- Priority: make the audience and practical outcome unmistakable in the first frame and caption.

Facebook — priority: context-rich explanation and discussion.
- Format: native video or image-plus-text post; include a short founder scenario and the verified product explanation. Cross-posting is allowed only after adapting the opening and CTA for clarity.
- Day 4 discussion prompt: “What important objective is hardest to keep moving when you are carrying the business yourself?” Label responses internally as exploratory qualitative input.
- Priority: explanatory copy and respectful replies; no claim about Facebook audience behavior is established.

X — priority: concise positioning and threaded explanation.
- Format: one short positioning post, followed by a 4–6 post thread on Day 1 or Day 3; use a reply question on Day 4 and a concise recap on Day 7.
- Suggested opening: “Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams—not a replacement for the founder.”
- Thread structure: who it is for; why generic AI-tool language can be unclear (this is a company hypothesis, not audience research); what Somebody does; what it does not guarantee; CTA.
- Priority: plain-language positioning and accurate replies. No claim about X engagement or posting-time trends is established.

5. Measurement and review guardrails

For every post, record channel, date/time, format, message variant, impressions/reach if available, profile visits, link clicks, signups, replies, and qualitative questions. These are measurement fields, not pre-existing facts.

Review after Day 3 and Day 7. Compare like-for-like formats and slots; do not infer audience preference from a single post. Treat all conclusions about engagement, audience behavior, or founder language as unknown until supported by collected analytics or documented qualitative research. Do not publish a “winning” claim during this draft phase.

6. Approval checklist before execution

- Confirm destination URL and signup flow.
- Approve any product screens, customer examples, founder scenarios, and claims used in creative.
- Confirm local timezone and analytics access.
- Confirm brand, accessibility, privacy, and reply-moderation requirements.
- Obtain review approval; this document itself does not publish or send anything.

Source register
- Company record: Company profile — company/profile.
- Company record: Launch brief — launch/context.
- No public or internal source in scope verifies platform-specific audience behavior, engagement trends, or optimal posting times; those items remain explicitly unknown.
deliverables.recommendedNextMove: Document current public or internal research for each platform, including source dates, coverage, extracted findings, and limitations, then revise or explicitly qualify the channel priorities and format recommendations against that evidence before treating the plan as launch-week ready.
